Use options.worksheet for an explicit choice, options.workflow?.source.worksheet for explicit workflow reuse, and this.workflow?.source.worksheet only when no source run is active (the activated-workflow case). findings.title: Fresh workbooks silently reuse the previous worksheet
findings.why_it_matters: After a user selects a sheet and configures a run, uploading another multi-sheet workbook inherits the old worksheet name. If the name exists, the new workbook is imported without a choice and may produce results from the wrong sheet. If it does not exist, the import fails without offering the available sheets. This is a silent wrong-result or missing-result path for replacement uploads.

findings.title: Worksheet choice leaks into the next workbook
findings.why_it_matters: After choosing a source worksheet, a later multi-sheet destination template can open with that same sheet name already selected. If the user proceeds without making a fresh template choice, headers come from the coincidentally named sheet in the template. This defeats the template's independent worksheet choice and can replace the output mapping with unintended headers.

learnings:
## Institutional Learnings Search Results

Search covered both files in docs/solutions and found one directly relevant entry: docs/solutions/xlsx-qualification.md.

Known Pattern: Qualify Excel archives before flattening cells (best_practice, inferred). Preserve raw/display/type/format/epoch/formula-cache data. Check actual expansion, CRC, central/local consistency and dangerous XML ranges before SheetJS parses the unchanged archive. U1 reproduced an alternate worksheet target bypass at xl/custom.xml. File-size checks, declared lengths and watchdogs do not establish allocation bounds.

Current src/formats/xlsx.ts:48 invokes preserved preflight before workbook reads, and selected-sheet parsing retains metadata. No contradiction was observed. The integrated worker, privacy, ordinary workbook compatibility and 10,000-row pipeline need U9 evidence. Historical driver guidance favors base64/indexed decoding over a 25 MiB JS number array.
